name: Xavier Becerra
role: U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services (2021–2025); California Democratic nominee for governor (2026)
summary: Becerra is a Democrat who spent 24 years in the U.S. House, then served as California attorney general and Biden's health secretary. His record is progressive on health care, abortion, LGBT rights, immigration and the environment, with a cautious record on trade and a mixed one on policing and the death penalty.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Said in 1994 he supported the single-payer plan, backed Medicare for All through his House years and said in 2017 he would support Sanders' bill; in 2019 called himself a single-payer advocate all his life.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Backed raising the federal minimum wage to $10.10 by 2016 (2013), a rise of about 40 percent over the then $7.25.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Quoted as saying tax cuts for millionaires take from schools and services; a progressive-tax group rated his votes 100 percent. No specific rate proposal found.

unions-good.rationale: Backed card-check union formation (2009); rated 87 percent by the AFL-CIO and 100 percent by the UFCW.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Sponsored enforcement against corporate offshore tax-haven banking (2013) and as AG led or joined antitrust and consumer actions against a hospital chain, Facebook and Amazon.

cut-welfare.rationale: Supported full funding of Head Start, Job Corps and WIC (1993) and criticised Trump-era HHS cuts in 2025 as a manmade disaster.

limit-guns.rationale: As AG led a 2020 suit demanding ATF regulate unfinished frames and receivers (ghost guns) as firearms, saying they are untraceable weapons used in mass shootings; rated F by the NRA. No statement on strict limits on ownership itself.

empower-police-military.rationale: Said in 2025 he would invest in local law enforcement, but also sought to reduce bias and unnecessary force in policing (2020); critics said he resisted police-record disclosure.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Stated support for marriage equality and opposition to the Defense of Marriage Act (2020); backed ENDA (2009).

abortion-legal.rationale: Rated 100 percent by NARAL and Planned Parenthood; said abortion funding avoids discrimination against poor women and backed a constitutional right; after Dobbs directed HHS to expand abortion-related care where possible.

free-trade.rationale: Mixed record: voted for NAFTA in 1993 and later said he regretted it; opposed fast-track and CAFTA; opposed permanent MFN for China; supported some pacts such as Peru. Rated 39 percent by Cato.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Asked in 2026 about phasing out fossil fuels he answered 'Absolutely' and cited defending clean car standards; backed 50 percent clean electricity by 2030 (2016); as AG sued over federal fossil fuel leasing and rollbacks.

school-vouchers.rationale: Recorded in 2015 as opposing private and religious school voucher programs; rated 100 percent by the NEA.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: In 2025 said he would avoid cutting health insurance for undocumented immigrants.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Opposed drilling in ANWR (2001), voted to ban offshore drilling in the Gulf (2016), sued over federal oil and gas leasing as AG, and in 2026 agreed with phasing out fossil fuels.

death-penalty.rationale: Voted in 2016 to repeal California's death penalty and in 2020 voiced serious reservations, yet as AG defended and pursued capital sentences under state law. Evidence points both ways.

ban-cartels.rationale: As California AG brought an antitrust suit against a hospital chain and joined the 2020 antitrust suit against Facebook; as HHS Secretary announced a plan to break up the organ transplant monopoly (2023).

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Backed stronger prohibitions on animal fighting (2007).

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: In 2002 rejected proposals for private Social Security savings accounts.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Voted yes in 2014 on authorizing training and equipping vetted Syrian opposition elements.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Said in 2020 he supports protecting transgender students and adults (a 2016 record item on not elevating gender identity as a protected class conflicts; the 2020 position is later).

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Backed repeal of Don't Ask Don't Tell and reinstatement of discharged gay service members (2010).

recognise-genocide.rationale: Backed official U.S. acknowledgement of the Armenian Genocide (2007, 2009).

voter-id.rationale: In 2014 said photo ID requirements to vote suppress the vote.

notes: Positions taken as AG and HHS Secretary were mostly his own litigation or administration priorities; only statements he made himself were used. Some OnTheIssues items are secondary summaries.
